title: Msiexec remote web package installation command
description: Detects Msiexec installation or administrative-install commands whose package argument is HTTP or HTTPS. URL properties on local packages are excluded and a .msi URL suffix is not required.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use Msiexec to retrieve and execute a remote installer package through a signed Windows binary.
hypothesis.rationale: Windows Installer accepts package sources via /i, /package and /a. The remote package need not expose a .msi URL suffix, and a local MSI may receive a harmless URL as a property; binding the URL to the package argument separates these cases.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify HTTP or HTTPS package arguments attached to /i, /package or /a, including extensionless endpoints; exclude URL properties on local MSI installation and unrelated text.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the remote package source and installation owner before escalation; enterprise deployment tooling can legitimately install MSI packages from managed web locations.
steps: Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the complete command, URL, package name, account, initiating process and effective original filename.
Inspect DNS, network and file events for the package, then validate its signer, hash, installation actions and spawned processes.
Confirm the URL and package with the responsible software-deployment owner; scope exceptions to an approved source and package identity rather than Msiexec globally.
false_positives: Approved software deployment or repair workflows that install signed MSI packages from managed HTTP or HTTPS repositories

validation.expected_outcome: Match web package arguments for install operations including extensionless URLs; reject local MSI plus URL property, URL-only text and non-install operations.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
